Increases EXP gained when an attack hits
or shoots down an enemy.

Increases funds gained for downing an
enemy.

Adds +1 max range to all weapons
except MAP and range 1.
Lowers the EN cost of using weapons.

Increases final damage dealt to the
enemy.

Reduces final damage taken from the
enemy.
Raises unit and weapon terrain ratings.

Raises HP and EN recovery from terrain,
ship docking, squad bonuses, parts and
abilities.

Raises the activation rate of defensive
skills.

Nullifies P-type and R-type effects of
enemy attacks.
Grants the same effect as a special skill.

If the squad contains units with a repair
function, all squad units gain HP recovery
10% per repair unit.

If the squad has units with a resupply
function, all squad units gain EN recovery
10% per resupply unit.

If the squad contains a unit with jamming,
final hit and evasion rates gain +10%.

If the squad contains a unit with a
lifter, the squad gains the Air move type
and can fly.

Short for Level, a guide to a pilot's
strength. It rises with EXP, up to 99.
Higher levels improve stats and teach new
skills and spirit commands.

The pilot's morale. Higher Will means
more damage and defense, and more usable
weapons. It starts at 100 and ranges
from 50 to 150.

Pilot Points are earned by defeating enemies.
Spend them to improve pilots.
Squad members receive 75% of the PP earned.

Short for Spirit Points, shown as current
over max. Spirit commands consume SP.
Very few ways exist to recover it on a
map, so spend it wisely.

The EXP needed to reach the next level.
Each level requires 500 EXP. The
greater the level gap with the enemy, the
more EXP earned.

Short for Experience, earned by landing an
attack or counter and surviving, or by
using repair or resupply. Non-leaders
receive only 75%.

Total enemies shot down. Only the pilot
who reduces an enemy's HP to 0 gets
credit. At 50 kills a pilot becomes an
Ace and gains a <1> icon.

A bonus at 50 kills. Funds from downing
enemies become 1.2x and starting Will
+5. Funds cap at 2x, so even with Lucky
it stops there.

The six pilot stats affecting combat -
Melee, Ranged, Skill, Defense, Evade and
Hit. They grow with level at a rate set
by each pilot's growth type.

The pilot's melee attack ability. The
higher it is, the more damage melee-class
weapons deal.

The pilot's ranged attack ability. The
higher it is, the more damage ranged-class
weapons deal.

The pilot's piloting precision. Higher
Skill raises the critical rate and helps
skills judged by Skill gap, such as
Re-Attack and Blocking, to fire.

How well the pilot defends. The higher it
is, the more damage from enemy attacks is
reduced.

How well the pilot evades. The higher
this plus the unit's Mobility, the more
easily it dodges.

The pilot's accuracy. The higher this
plus the unit's Sight and the weapon's hit
bonus, the more easily attacks land.

The pilot's adaptation to each terrain,
ranked S to D. In battle what applies is
the unit's rating, from pilot and unit
ratings together.

Fires only when the pilot is a squad
leader, and applies to the whole squad. A
captain's version is called a captain
effect.

The skills a pilot has learned. A
conditional skill changes color when it
fires. Reaching set levels teaches new
skills or raises their level.

Commands that aid battle; up to five are
learned. Shown as Spirit (SP cost).
Using one costs that SP. Effects and
duration differ per command.

Shows which squad the unit belongs to. A
single digit means a battleship, two
digits a formed squad, and letters an
event squad.

Icons showing squad information.
<2> marks a battleship,
<4> marks a squad leader,
<3> marks a unit in an event squad.

The unit's size class, from largest <15>
down through <16> > <17> > <18> > <19>.
The smaller side gains hit and evade, the
larger a damage bonus.

The damage a unit can take; at 0 it is
shot down. Shown as current over max HP.
Lost HP is restored by repair units,
spirit commands or parts.

The energy a unit carries, spent on
weapons and movement. Shown as current
over max EN. Lost EN is restored by
resupply units, commands or parts.

Armor is how tough the unit is. The
higher it is, the less damage taken from
enemies. A pilot with high Defense aboard
uses it even better.

Mobility is the unit's agility. The
higher this plus the pilot's Evade, the
more easily the unit dodges enemy
attacks.

Sight is the unit's accuracy. The higher
this plus the pilot's Hit and the weapon's
hit bonus, the more easily attacks land.

The unit's adaptation to each terrain,
ranked S to D. In battle what applies is
the unit's rating, from pilot and unit
ratings together.

Move is how far a unit can travel. One
square normally costs 1 Move, but some
terrain costs more. That cost is called
the movement cost.

Move type is the terrain a unit can
travel. If Air, Land or Water is listed
it can change to that element. Air- or
land-only warships cannot.

Special abilities built into the unit.
Each unit can hold up to four. Abilities
with activation conditions change text
color while active.

The parts equipped to the unit. How many
can be equipped depends on the unit's part
slots, 1 to 4. Consumable parts vanish
when used from the Parts command.

Lights when the unit has a repair device.
It can use Repair to restore HP. Its
squad also recovers 10% of max HP at the
start of each ally phase.

Lights when the unit has a resupply
device. Resupply fully restores EN and
ammo for 10 Will. Its squad recovers
10% of max EN each ally phase.

Two barriers consume EN to protect the unit.
Nullify: damage within the barrier's limit becomes 0.
[31]Above that limit, full damage is taken.
Reduce[8]: cuts damage by the barrier's listed value.

Lights when the unit has special armor.
Like <21>, it protects against enemy attacks,
but may block special effects as well as damage.

Lights when the unit carries a sword.
With the Blocking skill, swords and
solid-round weapons may be nullified by
Cutting, by Skill difference.

Lights when the unit carries a shield.
Defend cuts damage to 40% instead of
60%. With Blocking this can also occur
outside Defend, by Skill.

This icon lights when the unit can
transform. It can use the Transform
command to change form and show different
performance.

Lights when the unit can use Combine to
merge several units into one powerful
unit. The paired Separate command returns
them to the originals.

Active Spirits appear in blue. Abbreviations:
Va:Valor[10]En:Endure[10]Wa:Wall[10]Fo:Focus[10]St:Strike[10]Ac:Accel
Sw:Swift[10]Aw:Awaken[10]Sn:Snipe[10]Pi:Pierce[10]Lu:Luck[10]Ga:Gain
So:Soul[18]Al:Alert[13]Me:Mercy[14]Di:Disrupt[14]An:Analyze

Left is Move, the unit's Move stat. Right
is move type - Air, Land and Water. White
means passable; a dash means Air
impossible, the rest hard.

The unit's terrain rating, from pilot and
unit ratings. Ranked S to D, with A as
standard (100%). Good adaptation
improves hit, evade and defense.

How many squares the unit can move at
once, and the terrain it moves well in. A
squad's move is the average of its units.
A lit Air means it can fly.

A gauge showing how many stages of Armor
upgrade have been done. The gain per
stage differs by unit.

A gauge showing how many stages of
Mobility upgrade have been done.

A gauge showing how many stages of Sight
upgrade have been done. The gain per
stage differs by unit.

The weapon's name. The icon at left is
its class: <5> is a melee weapon, <6> is
a ranged weapon.

The weapon type. Besides normal
single-target weapons: <9> squad attack,
<10> hits a whole squad, <8> Tri Charge,
<11> all in range, <22> combined.

The weapon's traits. <14>: adds a status
effect on top of damage. <12>: usable
after moving. <13>: a beam weapon,
blockable by some barriers.

The weapon's attack power. The higher it
is, the more damage it deals. Upgrading a
weapon raises it.

The weapon's attack range, shown as
minimum to maximum. Snipe or a
high-performance radar can extend it.
Range 1 weapons cannot be extended.

How easily the weapon hits. It adjusts
hit rate along with the unit's Sight and
the pilot's Hit, so a higher value lands
attacks more easily.

Short for critical rate bonus, how easily
a critical hit occurs for 1.25x
damage. The rate is set by the Skill gap
with the enemy and the weapon's CRT.

How many times the weapon can fire,
current over max. Each use spends 1; at
0 it cannot be used. Resupply, a
Cartridge or docking refills it.

The EN spent when the weapon is used,
shown as cost (current EN). Below that
value it cannot be used. EN recovers via
commands, Resupply or terrain.

The Will needed to use the weapon, shown
as required (current). If Will has not
reached it, the requirement is shown in
red to mark it unusable.

The special skill and level needed to use
the weapon. Unless the main pilot has
learned that skill, the weapon cannot be
used.

Weapon terrain ratings run from S through A, B, C
and -. They affect damage against targets in that
terrain. A weapon rated Sea C, for example, deals
poor damage to an underwater enemy.

Effects that damage more than HP. They
split broadly into two kinds.
P-type: effects that act on the pilot.
R-type: effects that act on the unit.

Some weapons have these. Barrier Pierce:
damage ignores barriers, with exceptions.
Ignore Size: ignores size-based
reduction. Some skills nullify them.

A gauge showing how many stages of weapon
upgrade have been done. Cost per stage
differs by unit, and the attack gain
differs by weapon.

Whether the weapon counts as melee or
ranged. This decides which pilot stat is
used to compute its attack power.

The weapon's full name, with model
number.

Whether a MAP weapon can tell friend from
foe.
Valid hits only enemies in range; Invalid
hits both allies and enemies in range.

The shape of a MAP weapon's area.
Directional: a line in one of four
directions. Targeted: an area around a
point in range. Self: around your unit.

The squad's Move over move type. Move is
the average of each unit's, rounded down.
Type is white if all can move, grey if
some, blank if none.

The bonus to defense gained from being on
that terrain. Damage taken is reduced by
that rate.
No bonus applies while in the air.

The bonus to evasion gained from being on
that terrain. It is subtracted from the
enemy's final hit rate. No bonus applies
while in the air.

HP recovered at the start of the ally
phase while on that terrain. None
recovers in the air.

EN recovered at the start of the ally
phase while on that terrain. None
recovers in the air.

The formation the squad currently has
selected.
Battleships and single-unit squads show
none.

Support attack is possible. The icon
number is how many times it can be used.

Support defend is possible. The icon
number is how many times it can be used.

If even one unit in the squad has a repair
or resupply device, jamming or a lifter,
the effect applies to the whole squad.
This is a squad bonus.

At the start of the ally phase, each unit
in the squad recovers HP equal to 10% of
max per repair unit. It works only if a
unit in the squad has a repair device.

At the start of the ally phase, each unit
in the squad recovers EN equal to 10% of
max per resupply unit. It works only if a
unit in the squad has a resupply device.

Adds +10 to final hit and evade rates.
It works only if a unit in the squad has
jamming.

Adds Air to the squad's move type,
allowing flight.
It works only if a unit in the squad has a
lifter.

Shows current Spirit Points (SP). Spirit commands
consume SP to grant various benefits. Ways to
restore SP during a battle are very limited,
so use it effectively to avoid running out.

Sorts by battleship, event squad, then
squad number. Units that have acted show
in dark text. A status effect shows <24>,
docked units their ship.
Sorts by the original pilot order.
Sorts by pilot level, highest first.
The effect of the search item.
The target the spirit command is used on.

Gives spirit orders to chosen pilots at
once. <23> toggles each between reserved
(<25>) and not (<26>); <27> uses every
reserved command.

The spirit commands the pilot has
learned.
The special skills the pilot has learned.
Sorts by leader or captain effect order.
The special abilities the unit has.
Sorts by skill activation rate, desc.
Sorts by skill power, large to small.

The special gear needed for a squad
bonus.

Shows which squad bonus it belongs to, in
red.
Sorts units with a repair device first.
Sorts units with a resupply device first.

Sorts pilots who have learned Support
Attack first, by skill level descending.

Sorts pilots who have learned Support
Defend first, by skill level descending.

HP sorts by current HP, MAX by max HP,
descending.
Sorts by EXP needed to next level, desc.

Sorts by the attack power of the unit's
strongest weapon, descending.

The type and traits of the unit's
strongest weapon.
The main pilot aboard the unit.

Sorts by squad total current HP, descending.
<28> cycles the gauge maximum through
10000 / 20000 / 40000 / 80000.

Sorts by the squad's total current EN,
descending.
Sorts by the leader's current SP, desc.
Sorts by the leader's current Will, desc.
Sorts by member 1's current SP, desc.
Sorts by member 1's current Will, desc.
Sorts by member 2's current SP, desc.
Sorts by member 2's current Will, desc.
Sorts by the leader's kills, desc.
Sorts squads with a repair device first.

Sorts squads with a resupply device
first.

Sorts squads that have learned Support
Attack first, by skill level descending.

Sorts squads that have learned Support
Defend first, by skill level descending.

Sorts by the attack power of the leader's
strongest weapon, descending.

Sorts by the PLA weapon power of member
1.

Sorts by the PLA weapon power of member
2.

Sorts by Tri Charge attack power, the
average of the three TRI weapons,
descending. Some pilot combinations in a
squad raise Tri Charge power.

The conditions for ending the battle map.
Events or passing turns can change them or
add new ones. The objective screen shows
the latest.

The conditions that cause a game over.
Events or passing turns can change them or
add new ones. The objective screen shows
the latest.

The conditions for an SR Point, which
affects difficulty. Until they can be met
they show as ???. Only 1 SR Point is
earned per scenario.

Turns elapsed since this battle map
began.

Total turns elapsed since Episode 1
began.
Funds earned since this battle map began.
The total funds you currently hold.
BS earned since this battle map began.
The total BS you currently hold.

Whether the SR Point for this scenario has
been earned. Shows Not Earned if not,
Earned if so.

The number of squads each side has
deployed on the map. Allies in blue,
enemies in red.

How many enemy units were downed on this
battle map. <27> opens the detailed kill
list.

How many ally units were downed on this
battle map. <27> opens the detailed kill
list.

The parts obtained by downing enemies on
this battle map.
Sorts by kills on this battle map, desc.
Sorts by repair cost owed, descending.

Reserve squads with <23>, then <27> to
apply all. The mark is <26> normally and
<25> when reserved. If it matches the
formation it becomes <29>.

Short codes for the current formation.
T - Tri Formation
C - Center Formation
W - Wide Formation
Marks the side that is attacking.
Marks the side that is defending.

Units joining support attack and support
defend, with uses left and the support hit
rate.

The unit chose a normal attack with no
type label.

The unit chose to defend. Defending cuts
damage taken to 60%. With a shield
equipped it drops to 40%. Cutting and
afterimage still work while defending.

The unit chose to evade. Evading halves
the enemy's hit rate. If the computed hit
rate is over 100%, it will not drop to
50% but stay higher.
The unit chose to stand by.
The unit will attack with Tri Charge.
The unit will use an all-out attack.
The unit will use a combination attack.
The unit is joining a combination attack.

The unit will use a <35> combination
attack.
The unit will join the squad attack.

For some reason, such as low Will or a
range mismatch, the unit will not or
cannot join the squad attack.

The unit will not take part in this
battle.

The unit will cover an ally with support
defend.
The one covered is shown by a purple
arrow.

A unit able to support defend will not
cover an ally.

The unit is defenseless, taking neither
evade nor defend.

The unit is unable to fight. It cannot join
attacks or counters, but can still choose evade
or defend.
Chooses to receive no support attack.

The selected weapon's cost EN (current
EN).

Hit rate if you attack with the chosen
weapon.

A guide to how much damage the supporting
unit will take. <34> x2: risk of being
shot down <34> x1: risk if a critical
lands <34> x0: no risk

The EXP earned in this battle. Downing an
enemy gives the sum of the unit and pilot
values. A hit gives one tenth, and
non-leaders receive 75%.

The PP earned in this battle. PP for
downing an enemy differs by unit, and
non-leaders receive 75%.

The pilot's current level. If EXP earned
raises it, this shows current level to new
level. Press <27> to go to the level-up
screen.

Shows current level to new level. Items
that changed with the level-up blink in
their frame.

A newly learned special skill, or one
whose skill level rose, is shown in
green.

A newly learned spirit command is shown in
green.

If a value rose with the level-up, the
gain is shown in green at the right. If
two or more levels rose at once, the
totals are shown.

If a value rose with the level-up, the
name shows in bright blue and the gain in
green at the right. If several levels
rose, totals are shown.

Sorts by all-unit setting, squad BGM, then
unit order.

Sorts by battleship, event squad, squad
number, then reserve.

Shows maximum Spirit Points (SP). Spirit commands
consume SP to grant various benefits. Ways to
restore SP during a battle are very limited,
so use it effectively to avoid running out.

For each terrain, sorts units whose move
type is passable (white) first.
Sorts units with special armor first.
Sorts units with a barrier first.

Gauges showing how many upgrade stages have been
done for HP, EN, Armor, Mobility, Sight and
weapons.

Shows how far the unit's stats have been
upgraded. Taking HP, EN, Armor, Mobility
and Sight to the top stage makes 100%
and unlocks a bonus.

Shows how many stages the weapons have
been upgraded. For weapons the stage is
labeled RANK.

Sorts pilots who have learned Commander
first, by skill level descending.

Sorts by the pilot stat Melee,
descending.

Sorts by the pilot stat Ranged,
descending.

Sorts by the pilot stat Skill,
descending.

Sorts by the pilot stat Defense,
descending.

Sorts by the pilot stat Evade,
descending.
Sorts by the pilot stat Hit, descending.

For each terrain, sorts pilot terrain
